anchors.paper_title: MNE-BIDS: Organizing electrophysiological data into the BIDS format and facilitating their analysis
anchors.paper_venue: The Journal of Open Source Software
anchors.reason: MNE-BIDS is a software tool for organizing electrophysiology data into BIDS, used for dataset conversion, not a paper describing this motor imagery dataset.

anchors.paper_title: EEG-BIDS, an extension to the brain imaging data structure for electroencephalography
anchors.reason: EEG-BIDS is a specification/standard extension to BIDS for EEG, used to organize this dataset, not a paper describing this motor imagery dataset.

metadata.methods_description: Cue-based offline motor imagery paradigm with left-hand grasping, right-hand grasping and foot hooking imagery. Each subject performed 90 trials (30 per class), stored as 4 s epochs. EEG was recorded with a Neuracle 64-channel wireless amplifier (59 EEG channels, 10-10 montage) at 1000 Hz, with 50 Hz line frequency.
